key_insight: Clifford template compilation has a sharp complexity split: some commuting cases are efficiently solvable, while binary or bounded variants become NP-complete, and certain recovery tasks even touch quantum-classical advantage via discrete logarithms.
engineering_relevance: For quantum error correction and constrained circuit synthesis, this work tells engineers when template-based Clifford search is tractable, when quantum algorithms may help, and when compilation is provably hard.
method: Analyze the inverse problem of matching a target Pauli transformation by choosing repetition counts in a Clifford template.
Classify complexity across template types: commuting vs noncommuting, unrestricted integers vs binary exponents, and bounded-total-count variants.

Identify algorithmic/complexity frontiers: NP∩BQP for some commuting integer-exponent cases, classical poly-time for self-inverse commuting binary cases, and NP-completeness in several restricted settings.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical complexity results and constructive algorithms, including a quantum polynomial-time procedure that returns a solution and exponent-relation lattice for commuting templates, plus NP-completeness proofs for restricted variants.
watch_item: These are worst-case complexity results, so practical compiler performance will still depend on template structure, instance size, and hardware/fault-tolerance constraints.
paper_title: Computational Complexity of Clifford Template Compilation: Are Quantum Computers Useful for Compiling Quantum Circuits?
